Jacob, saw Streamline joined CivicPlus late last year, which opens up a much wider special-districts market to sell into.

A bigger addressable market usually means more districts in play than reps can cover before they ramp. Our AI SDR researches, writes, and follows up autonomously, so coverage scales without new hires: 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Streamline off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?

Jacob, quick follow-up for Streamline.

Post-acquisition, the pipeline target on the sales team usually jumps faster than headcount can. Most teams don't actually know how many meetings they need to book to hit the new number, so the gap shows up late and the quarter becomes a scramble.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I'll walk you through our pipeline model and show exactly how many meetings Streamline needs this quarter, and where the math breaks if you only add reps.
email.body3:
Jacob, last bit of proof for Streamline.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and couldn't hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks with every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Streamline's reply rate likely compares to other govtech software teams. Want to hop on a quick call and I'll walk you through it?
email.body4:
Jacob, I'll stop reaching out on this one, but didn't want to leave you empty-handed.

If scaling pipeline without adding headcount isn't a focus while the CivicPlus integration settles, no problem at all. Combining two go-to-market motions is its own project.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to a special-districts motion? I'll tailor it to Streamline either way.
